subject: crush
title: Repeated-tool-call loop breaker: sha256 call signatures over a sliding window
one_why: Window 10, >5 identical tool-interaction signatures aborts the turn - cheap, testable, and the only anchor subject enforcing an anti-loop guard in core.

subject: crush
title: Hook pre-approval bound to one tool-call id via unexported context key
one_why: A PreToolUse hook granting approval cannot be replayed onto other calls sharing a context; the id-matching grant is the scoping primitive the seeded concept asks for.

subject: crush
title: Central permission service prompts per tool call and short-circuits only on scoped hook grants
one_why: Nuance vs cline-4: enforcement lives in a service the tool wrapper consults, not a hook chain ahead of policy.

subject: crush
title: No OS sandbox: approved bash executes with full user privileges
evidence: no sandbox module under internal/ (grep); permission prompts are the sole barrier (internal/permission/permission.go)
one_why: Same hole as cline-7; third convergence - prompts-only safety is the corpus default and the clearest roadmap gap class.

subject: crush
title: agent.go (2393 LOC) and coordinator.go (1877 LOC) fuse loop, policy, and tool wiring
one_why: Auto-summarize triggers, channel provenance, and provider options all sit in one file; boundary extraction is where this codebase's test-ability ceiling comes from.

subject: crush
title: recover() middleware at server, shell runner, and logger boundaries
one_why: Panic containment at each trust boundary keeps a crashing tool from killing the TUI or server socket - the minimal crash posture for a long-lived process.

subject: crush
title: Turns carry their originating channel in context so remote-originated turns are distinguishable
one_why: Context-tagged provenance (herdr/remote vs local) lets policies and UI treat remote-driven turns differently without a separate code path.
